facts.raw_span: progressive dyspnea on exertion
multiple prior cardiac events
lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery
denied chest pain
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T (hs-cTnT) level was 40 ng/L
Normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
1.0-mm ST elevation in lead V1
4.0-mm ST elevation in leads V2 and V3
Well-circumscribed 2.8 × 2.6-cm mass located in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade
Nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

concepts.why: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and a well-circumscribed mass is located in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum.
The patient has a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade.
The patient has an elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level and ST elevation in leads V2 and V3, indicating myocardial injury.
The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium.

rationales.F03: Lung cancer with metastatic disease to the myocardium increases the likelihood of cardiac metastasis.
rationales.F10: A well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricle is highly suggestive of cardiac metastasis.
rationales.F11: A large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade is a strong indicator of cardiac tamponade.

frontier_selector.rationale: Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade and the patient's progressive dyspnea on exertion
